_comment: The GitHub issue forms ErgoptiPlus opens (Debug > Report a bug, Suggest a feature). `file` names a form of .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and every id in `fields` must be one of its fields (tools/test/test-issue-templates.cjs); `fields` also declares the URL builder's field order and truncation order. Diagnostic reporters prefill the host-derived version, driver (a dropdown option: macOS, Windows or Linux) and os values and the compact approved report (readable English lines grouped most useful first, no JSON block) in `report_field`, which is the last declared field so the budget cuts it first; a cut report ends with the truncation marker and one note saying the complete report is on the clipboard, to paste into `full_report_field` (share_policy.truncated_note_key of schema.json). `full_report_field` names the required textarea the user pastes the complete approved report into, copied to the clipboard and saved locally by the report action; it is never prefilled and so is not in `fields`. The report action copies it bounded to full_report_max_bytes UTF-8 bytes (a byte is at most one character, so the bound holds however GitHub counts): a longer report keeps its first whole lines and ends with the truncation marker and the note of share_policy.full_report_cut_note_key, while the saved file stays complete. max_issue_body_chars is GitHub's limit on an issue body; full_report_max_bytes leaves room under it for max_url_bytes of prefilled fields, the form's headings and the user's own text (checked in tools/test/test-issue-templates.cjs). With every manifest setting of the Linux driver changed (340 rows), the complete report measured 45,773 bytes on 2026-11-24. `day_log_field` names the optional textarea where the user drops the redacted day log the app saved; it is never prefilled and so is not in `fields`. The repository comes from _shared/updater/data/defaults.json, never from here. max_url_bytes bounds the percent-encoded URL and max_redirect_bytes the login redirect of a signed-out click, login_redirect_prefix then the URL encoded again (each %XX becomes %25XX), so a letter-dense report keeps the whole URL budget and a dense one is cut sooner. Measured anonymously with tools/dev/measure-issue-url-limits.cjs on 2026-11-24: /issues/new answered 500 from about 6,460 bytes and /login from about 6,500, so a 4,000-byte URL dense in %XX (a 6,670-byte redirect) failed; the redirect budget keeps about 1,500 bytes for a browser's own headers and cookies (limits checked in tools/test/test-issue-templates.cjs). Built by _shared/ui/issue_link.js and its Lua and AHK ports.
